methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $380M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
ZeroAvia, a Series C-stage Transportation company founded by Valery Miftakhov, has raised $380M+ to date. The Transportation sector comprises 8 private comparables (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and Harbinger) and no public peers suitable for direct valuation benchmarking.

A stage-progression method provides the primary valuation anchor. Using total capital raised ($380M) as a proxy for cumulative value creation and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C progression yields $646M. This reflects the empirical pattern of capital multipliers between rounds in frontier transportation infrastructure. A peer-median approach was not applicable: while Transportation as a sector contains 3 comparable companies, the narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, and similar-tier valuations returned zero datapoints meeting the minimum threshold of three observations. Broadening to all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of business models and maturity levels within the peer set.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $549M (low) to $743M (high), with a central estimate of $646M. This range reflects the bounds of stage-typical multiple variation around the primary method. Key uncertainties include the absence of close-stage comparable valuations in the narrow peer universe and reliance on capital-raised as a proxy for creation value rather than market-based pricing signals. Terminal assumptions regarding development timelines and route-to-profitability remain material unresolved factors.
